rules.name: House Rules Check

mustBe: Disclosed in the House rules and requests section of the listing before booking (no new rules later by message, signs or in person)
Consistent with the rest of the listing
Compliant with Airbnb policies: no separate contracts or personal info such as government ID, except where required by law and other limited circumstances
generallyNotAllowed: Tasks a cleaner would do or that take significant effort: stripping beds, taking trash off-site, washing and putting away dishes
Restricting a feature advertised as part of the listing; fees for advertised features must be in the price at booking
Fines or other penalties (damage: AirCover; HOA/local fines: notice in the Local rules section)
allowedExamples: Sort trash into designated indoor bins
Local exceptions such as animal-proof bins or drought shower limits

minpaku.law: 住宅宿泊事業法 art. 8 + MLIT guideline (最終改正 2024-12-24)
items: foreign guests without a Japan address: nationality (国籍) and passport number (旅券番号), see the passport and keep a copy (旅券の写し) with the register
minpaku.notes: Identity must be confirmed before the stay, face-to-face or by ICT (e.g. a tablet or video call at the property). Contact details are recommended, not required. Keep the register 3 years.

ryokan.law: 旅館業法 art. 6 + 施行規則 art. 4-2
items: foreign guests without a Japan address: nationality (国籍) and passport number (旅券番号)
ryokan.notes: MHLW guidance also asks hotels and ryokan to see and copy the passport of foreign guests without a Japan address. Keep the register 3 years.

japan.explanationDuty: 住宅宿泊事業法 art. 9: explain noise, trash and fire-prevention points; in a foreign language for foreign guests.
japan.trash: MLIT guideline: minpaku trash is business waste the operator must dispose of; guests leave sorted trash at the designated place in the home.

rules.disclaimer: Educational pattern check, not legal advice and not affiliated with or endorsed by Airbnb. Findings are likely outcomes from keyword rules based on Airbnb's public help article and announcement (as of 2026-10-28), not Airbnb's decision; Airbnb's own listing editor and support decide. Japan notes summarise the 住宅宿泊事業法, 旅館業法 rules and the MLIT guideline; confirm with your local health centre (保健所) or a professional.

rules.summary: Since 2026-05-29 Japan's heavy-rain, flood, landslide and storm-surge warnings carry the alert level in their name: Level 5 特別警報 Emergency Warning (black), Level 4 危険警報 Urgent Warning (purple, new), Level 3 警報 Warning (red), Level 2 注意報 Advisory (yellow), Level 1 早期注意情報 Early Advisory (white). Evacuate by Level 4. Earthquake Early Warnings, tsunami warnings, Nankai Trough information, J-ALERT and the other weather warnings keep their names.

alerts.issuedBy: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA); pushed to every phone in the area by the carriers (loud buzzer), plus TV and radio
alerts.meaning: An earthquake has just started and strong shaking (seismic intensity 5-lower or more, or long-period ground motion class 3+) is predicted. JMA sends it when two or more seismometers detect the quake; the areas named expect intensity 4 or more. You have seconds to tens of seconds, or none if you are near the epicentre. It is a prediction: real shaking can be stronger or weaker, and it does not say exactly when shaking arrives.
doNow: Protect yourself first: take cover under a sturdy table or desk and protect your head.
Stay away from windows, shelves, TVs and anything that can fall.
Do not rush outside and do not try to put out fires until the shaking stops.
Tell people around you.
When the shaking stops: if you are near the coast, check for a tsunami warning; then check for fire and gas.

doNow: Check your area on KIKIKURU and evacuate early if you are in a danger area.
If it is dark or roads are already flooded, move to a higher floor instead.

doNow: Get ready to evacuate now while it is still safe, especially near slopes or rivers.

alerts.meaning: Rain of a once-in-several-years intensity has been observed within about an hour. Disasters may be happening nearby. Formerly 記録的短時間大雨情報.
doNow: Check KIKIKURU; if your area is purple or black, take safety action now.
Avoid underpasses, basements and rivers.

doNow: If the sky darkens suddenly or you hear thunder or a roar, go inside a sturdy building, away from windows.

doNow: Avoid driving; if you are stuck, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow.

alerts.meaning: A disaster is happening or imminent. Going to a shelter may already be dangerous. It is not always issued, so don't wait for it.
doNow: Take the safest action immediately: go to the highest floor or the room furthest from a slope.
Only move outside if that is safer than staying.

alerts.meaning: Everyone in the named danger area must evacuate now. Since 2021 there is no separate 避難勧告 (evacuation advisory); 避難指示 is the one to act on.
doNow: Evacuate now to a designated shelter or a safe place outside the danger area (a friend's house or a hotel counts).
If it is already dangerous outside, move up to a higher floor.

doNow: If you or someone with you needs time: go now.

assumptions: Alcohol is assessed by volume: 3 bottles × 760 ml = 2280 ml per adult. If you give only a bottle count, each bottle is assumed to be 760 ml. When drinks of different types exceed the allowance, the allowance is applied to the highest-rate drink first (Customs chooses in the traveler's favor).
Heat-not-burn: 10 individual packages = 200 sticks (IQOS / glo, 20 per pack) or 50 capsules (Ploom TECH / with type, 5 per pack), per Japan Customs' own examples.

More than one kind of tobacco: the English rule says the total allowance is 250 g. For that reading we use cigarette ≈ 1 g, cigar ≈ 5 g, heat-not-burn stick ≈ 1 g, heat-not-burn capsule ≈ 4 g (one pack ≈ 20 cigarettes), cap each kind at its single-kind allowance, and use the 250 g on cigars / other tobacco first, then cigarettes and sticks, then capsules. Japan Customs' own worked example (zeigaku.htm) instead exempts only the one most favorable kind in full and taxes the rest, so the high estimate uses that stricter reading.
Perfume: 2 oz ≈ 56 ml (1 oz ≈ 28 ml). Eau de toilette and eau de cologne are not counted as perfume (menzei.htm).

Other goods: a line (one kind of item) whose total overseas value is ¥10,000 or less is free and not counted (menzei.htm: 1品目ごとの合計額が1万円以下). Each article worth more than ¥200,000 is fully dutiable. The ¥200,000 is then filled with the articles that save the most duty (best-subset search).

Customs value = overseas retail price × 0.6 (zeigaku.htm). Simplified 15% applies to that Customs value; articles whose Customs value exceeds ¥100,000 (overseas price above about ¥166,667) use the general tariff and are not estimated. Duty-free-tariff articles (wristwatches, golf clubs, PCs, loose gemstones, paintings) pay 10% consumption tax only.

Rounding follows the official example: yen are truncated per line, then each tax type (liquor tax, tobacco tax, customs duty, consumption tax) is truncated to ¥100; the consumption tax base is truncated to ¥1,000.
travelers multiplies the per-person allowance and assumes everyone is in the same age band; articles are pooled. Run minors separately for an exact split.

rules.title: Japan dual pricing (二重価格): resident vs non-resident prices at tourist sites
keyFacts: Dual pricing in Japan is legal and set by each facility; the Japan Tourism Agency (観光庁) runs a study group (first meeting 2026-04-27) and plans guidelines for public facilities within FY2026 (by March 2027).

The test is almost always residence (registered address in the city/prefecture, or living in Japan), not nationality. Foreign residents with a registered address pay the resident price; Japanese visitors from other cities pay the higher price.

Two kinds: A = surcharge aimed at visitors (Himeji Castle, Nanzoin, JUNGLIA, Nara Prison Museum, Nijo Castle and Kyoto City Bus plans); B = discount for local residents (Odawara Castle, Kitakyushu, Kagoshima City, Sapporo TV Tower).
Proof: usually a My Number card, driver's license, health insurance card or residence card showing the address; without proof you pay the general price.

Announced, not in force: Nijo Castle (¥1,000 citizens / ¥2,000 others, FY2027), Kyoto City Bus (¥200 citizens / ¥360 others, FY2027), national museums (higher price for non-residents by March 2031). Under review: Kenrokuen (first committee meeting 2026-10-14). Dropped: Osaka Castle (one price ¥1,200).

steps: Microchip ISO 11784/11785 (15 digits), on or before the first rabies shot. 900202… chips not accepted; some 900-prefix chips duplicated: notify AQS early.
Rabies vaccine #1 at 91+ days old (birth = day 0), after the chip; inactivated or recombinant only (no live / RNA).
Vaccine #2: 30+ days after #1 (#1 = day 0) and within #1's effective period (duration of immunity).
Blood draw on or after the #2 day, within the vaccine's effective period; MAFF-designated lab; ≥0.5 IU/ml; valid 2 years from the draw.
Wait 180 days from the draw (draw = day 0) in the exporting country. Arrival also within the antibody validity and vaccine effective period (boosters on time).
Advance notification to AQS at the arrival port 40+ days before arrival (NACCS / email). Later notices in principle not accepted; arrival cannot be moved earlier.
Clinical inspection within 10 days before boarding (rabies; dogs also leptospirosis); government-endorsed certificate (Form AC).
Import inspection on arrival: ≤12 h if all is in order; otherwise detention up to 180 days (or shipped back), importer pays.
importFromNonDesignatedRegions.earlyArrival: Arriving before the 180 days are up: detention for the remaining days (not counting arrival and release days). No medical exceptions.
importFromNonDesignatedRegions.antibodyExpired: New draw at a designated lab before the 2-year validity ends; no new waiting period if the vaccine chain is unbroken.

importFromDesignatedRegions.rule: Microchip, residence (since birth / 180+ days immediately before export / since coming directly from Japan; otherwise detention for 180 minus days resident), 40-day notice, clinical inspection within 10 days before boarding, Form AB, direct transport or seal / ANNEX. No vaccine, antibody test or 180-day wait.

exportFromJapan.rule: Apply for export inspection to AQS at least 14 days before export (NACCS or email; up to 3 preferred times in remarks); inspection within 10 days before departure unless the destination says otherwise. Check the destination's entry rules with its embassy.

shortStayAbroad.rule: Leaving Japan and coming back: do microchip, 2 rabies shots and the antibody test (≥0.5 IU/ml) in Japan before departure → no 180-day wait abroad, ≤12 h quarantine on return within 2 years of the draw (boosters abroad on time; redraw abroad if the 2 years run out). 40-day notice before return and a vet check within 10 days before boarding abroad still apply.

specialPeriod.rule: If you applied for an extension or change of status before your period of stay ends (and your period is over 30 days) and no decision is made by the expiry date, you may stay until the decision or 2 months after the expiry date, whichever is first.
specialPeriod.leavingWhilePending: Allowed with a re-entry permit or deemed re-entry. With deemed re-entry, return by the earlier of 1 year from departure or 2 months after the old expiry date, and receive the decision at the immigration office before those 2 months end (ISA Q&A Q61).

rules.shortTermVisitors: No deemed re-entry and, in principle, no re-entry permit (ISA Q&A Q62). Cruise exception: 15 days on a designated passenger ship (art. 26-3).

rules.summary: Japan's tax-free shopping for visitors switches on 2026-11-01 from tax-off-at-the-till to a refund method: pay the tax-inclusive price, get the consumption tax back after customs confirms on departure (before checking bags) within 90 days of purchase.

regimes.howItWorks: Eligible shops sell at the tax-exclusive price after checking your passport. Nothing to claim back later.
regimes.categories: General goods and consumables are separate; each needs ¥5,000+ before tax unless packed together. Consumables capped at ¥500,000 and sealed in special packaging.
regimes.atDeparture: Present your passport; customs may inspect the goods (after security, restricted area).

regimes.howItWorks: Pay the tax-inclusive price at a tax-free shop and register a refund method. On departure, scan your passport at a tax-free kiosk (or Visit Japan Web at major airports) BEFORE checking bags. Green = done; Red = customs inspection. After customs confirms, the shop or its refund operator pays back the consumption tax.
regimes.minimumPerStorePerDay: ¥5,000 before tax (same purchaser, same store, same day)
regimes.categories: No general/consumable split, no ¥500,000 cap, no sealed bags. Quantities limited to what you can carry out yourself. Consumables used in Japan are not refundable.
regimes.atDeparture: Final departure airport/seaport, international departure lobby, before baggage check-in.
regimes.deadline: Customs confirmation on departure within 90 days of purchase, counted from the day after purchase (bought 2026-11-01 -> by 2027-01-30).

taxMath.reducedRateCovers: Food and non-alcoholic drinks (not restaurant dining).

notEligible: Goods used or consumed in Japan before departure
rules.fees: The refund is paid by the tax-free shop or its refund operator (card, app, bank transfer, or cash at the port), not by customs. Japanese law sets no rule on refund fees, so the shop or operator may deduct a handling fee; you can receive less than maxRefundJPY.
checklist: Bring the passport you showed at purchase (cruise passengers and crew: also the landing permit).
Each store's purchases are added up per day: you need ¥5,000+ before tax at one store on one day.
Register your refund method (card, app, etc.) at the shop when you buy; ask how and when they pay.
Depart Japan within 90 days of the purchase date (counted from the day after purchase).

Do the tax-free kiosk (or Visit Japan Web at Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, New Chitose, Fukuoka, Naha) at your FINAL departure airport or seaport, BEFORE checking bags. Checked bags cannot be retrieved for this.
Carry every item from each receipt. If one item from a receipt is missing, nothing on that receipt is refunded.

Take all tax-free goods, general goods and consumables alike, out of Japan unused. Food, drinks, and cosmetics used in Japan are not refundable; if you used some, skip the kiosk and tell the customs counter.
Green result: done. Red result: take the goods to the customs inspection area before boarding. Leave plenty of time; missing your flight is not compensated.
Items costing ¥1,000,000+ before tax: bring the certificate of authenticity or warranty.
Export the goods without delay after customs confirms them, or the tax is collected back and penalties apply.
rules.disclaimer: Educational estimate, not tax advice. Rules can change; check the official sources. The tax-free shop, its refund operator, and Japan Customs decide eligibility and the amount you actually receive.
